text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Lennart Meri warned the Western nations about the possible consequences of the failure to admit the Baltic states into European structures during the first day of his three-day official visit to Hungary.
- The parliament voted in favour of a total ban on advertising tobacco products.
- The government will appoint Andra Veidemann as minister for ethnic relations. The post of minister for European reforms will be abolished.
- Estonian gas firms have agreed on a price rise.
- The government has decided to amend the law on language concerning direct TV broadcasts; the Estonian translation will be no longer be required.
- The government decided to impose income tax on offshore firms; a similar draft law was rejected last year as ineffective.
- The transport ministry is preparing a draft law lifting the speed limit to 100 kilometres per hour outside towns.
- Teachers who participated in Monday's strike have promised to take further action unless their demands are met.
- A man shot dead his 8-year-old son and wounded himself as a result of a domestic quarrel.
- The Savings Bank and Hansapank are exploring the possibility of buying stakes in Lithuania's Agricultural Bank.
